jobs.description:
Role: Enterprise Architecture Manager
Location: London, Manchester or Edinburgh
Mobility : Up to 100%
Career Level: Manager (ML7)

Industry Technology Strategy & Architecture (ITSA)

About ITSA
Industry Technology Strategy & Architecture leads at the intersection of business and technology, driving maximum client value through the exploitation of AI, technology and data. We serve as the primary architect of our clients' industry-relevant technology estate, defining future-state visions, building the business case for change, and designing the enterprise architecture that turns ambition into an executable roadmap.

Our work spans four solution areas: Business Technology Strategy, Technology Visioning / Future Tech & Innovation, Enterprise & Technology AI & Data Strategy, and Industry Enterprise Architecture. Across all of them we deliver measurable outcomes: full traceability between business priorities and technology investment, stronger investment alignment and prioritization, reduced architectural complexity and duplication, and faster identification of AI, data and digital opportunities.

Your responsibilities

- Own architecture workstreams and delivery within enterprise architecture engagements, shaping scope, mobilising teams, managing plans, risks, issues, client expectations and project commercials, and setting out clear implications, options and trade-offs.

- Assess how business strategy and industry trends drive the need for change across organisation, applications, data, infrastructure and operations.

- Define and co-create the enterprise architecture vision, target-state architecture and multi-year roadmaps, aligned to business objectives.

- Drive modernisation for the AI/intelligence era through application rationalisation and consolidation that reduces complexity and duplication.

- Build value cases and investment justifications aligned to client planning cycles, identifying levers such as cost reduction, technical-debt treatment and platform consolidation.

- Guide and conclude key architectural decisions across business, technology and third-party stakeholders in multi-vendor ecosystems.

- Apply and help mature enterprise architecture governance, frameworks and standards, including IT governance.

- Define enterprise data and AI platform, integration and automation strategies, including AI-enabled and agentic architectures, and create reusable assets, blueprints and accelerators.

- Build and sustain strong client relationships, including with senior stakeholders such as the Head of Enterprise Architecture, CTO and CIO.

- Support senior leadership in sales and origination by identifying and qualifying opportunities, shaping proposals and statements of work, and matching client needs to relevant Accenture offerings.

- Lead medium-to-large teams or work efforts, setting clear objectives and standards, coordinating and delegating work, and building an effective, positive team environment.

- Coach, mentor and develop team members through regular feedback and formal performance responsibilities, addressing development needs and contributing to hiring, staffing and resourcing decisions.

- Own the quality of documents, presentations, architecture outputs and other deliverables produced by the team, ensuring they are rigorous, coherent and ready to be presented to C-suite and executive-level audiences.

- Contribute to the growth and effective operation of the Accenture practice and ITSA by leading capability-building and community initiatives, supporting recruitment, sharing knowledge, developing reusable assets and thought leadership, and meeting internal business obligations.

We are looking for the following skills and experience

Core capabilities

- High-level thinking: pursue innovative approaches, synthesise complex information to surface trends and root causes, and stay effective amid ambiguity while keeping the bigger picture and client value in view.

- Execution: plan and prioritise to high standards, apply structured processes and quality reviews, and manage scope, cost and risk while working ethically and protecting data.

- Collaboration: build trusted, inclusive relationships and share knowledge across teams and clients, drawing on diverse perspectives to reach aligned outcomes.

- Communication: make complex ideas clear and audience-appropriate, surface risks constructively, and develop and deliver a compelling vision of the value created.

- Learning and development: model continuous learning and curiosity, coach and develop others through honest feedback, and evaluate outcomes to drive improvement.

Enterprise architecture skills

- Deep expertise across enterprise architecture strategy, enterprise architecture modelling and planning, architecture governance and architecture frameworks.

- Strong command of TOGAF or an equivalent framework, together with IT governance and IT service management principles.

- A track record of assessing and architecting enterprise-level solutions and IT portfolios end to end.

- Deep capability in application architecture design, application strategy, solution architecture, technology architecture assessment, blueprint and roadmap definition, and IT capability assessment.

Experience

- Relevant experience, including leading enterprise architecture engagements or programmes and establishing architecture governance.

Set yourself apart
We're very interested in hearing from you if you have some or all of the following.

- A track record of setting up or running an Enterprise Architecture function or office.

- Experience leading complex modernisation or AI-era transformation programmes.

- Professional-level cloud or platform architecture certifications (e.g. AWS, Azure or Google Cloud).

- Fluency with EA tooling and modelling standards (e.g. ArchiMate, LeanIX, Ardoq).

- Deep sector expertise in one or more industries.

- Recognised thought leadership or an active presence in the architecture community.

- An advanced degree such as an MBA or a relevant MSc.

What’s in it for you
At Accenture in addition to a competitive basic salary, you will also have an extensive benefits package, private medical insurance and 3 extra days leave per year for charitable work of your choice!

Role: Project Controls Consulting (Risk Management focus) - Infrastructure & Capital Projects
Career Levels: Consultant / Manager
Location: Hybrid from Dublin or Cork, Ireland (with occasional travel)

As a team:
In the Infrastructure & Capital Projects team, we shape how infrastructure is built and managed. We drive innovation by delivering the best-in-class management consultancy based on industrial experience maximised by the latest technologies. Infrastructure & Capital Projects is one of Accenture’s biggest global growth areas, shown by recent acquisitions announced in this area, and you will be joining at a pivotal moment of growth.

About us:
We help clients deliver some of the most complex energy, transport and infrastructure programmes by fusing industry risk expertise with advanced analytics, automation and cloud platforms. From portfolio risk intelligence to project-level decision support, our team uses AI‑augmented insight, digital twins, and interactive dashboards to improve confidence, compress decision cycles and drive better outcomes across EMEA.

The opportunity:
Join us to embed risk-by-design across development, design and construction—moving beyond traditional registers to predictive, data‑driven risk management. You’ll work in multidisciplinary squads with planners, commercial managers and engineers, leveraging QRA, scenario modelling and live data to inform contingency, confidence levels and executive decision-making. At Manager level, you’ll shape portfolio‑wide risk strategies, standards and digital enablement.

Key responsibilities:
Project & Programme Risk Management
- Lead/support risk processes aligned to agreed frameworks and digitally enabled workflows (e.g., integrated risk platforms, automated notifications).

- Facilitate structured risk workshops and drive data quality—linking risks to schedule, cost and commercial assumptions for traceability.

- Track emerging risks and mitigation performance with live KPIs; escalate against tolerances using visual risk signals.

Quantitative Risk Analysis (QRA) & Decision Support
- Deliver QRA/QSRA to inform contingency and confidence; translate qualitative risks into robust quantitative inputs and sensitivity models.

- Use predictive techniques and risk driver analysis to highlight what really matters; present decision‑ready insights in interactive formats for senior stakeholders.

- (Manager) Lead scenario modelling and options analysis; coach teams in QRA best practice.

Governance, Reporting & Assurance
- Run periodic risk reviews and portfolio forums; produce executive‑level summaries showing trends, exposure changes and return‑on‑mitigation.

- Ensure auditability and alignment between risk registers, cost plans, schedules and commercial baselines through integrated data models.

- (Manager) Set risk standards and portfolio reporting that scales across programmes and supply chains.

Stakeholder Engagement & Integration
- Act as a trusted advisor—embedding proportionate, value‑adding risk thinking into project and governance decisions.

- Partner closely with PMs, planners, commercial managers, designers and contractors to operationalise risk insights.

- (Manager) Mentor teams and uplift risk maturity across regions.

Continuous Improvement
- Analyse outcomes to identify themes; convert lessons learned into preventative controls, automation opportunities and stronger processes.

- Contribute to evolving risk guidance, tools, templates and training, including data standards and dashboards.

Experience we are looking for:
Essential:
- Proven capital project risk experience with strong facilitation skills across multi‑project environments.

- Solid knowledge of qualitative and quantitative risk techniques, including supporting QRA/QSRA activities.

- Ability to translate complex uncertainty into clear, actionable insight for project teams and stakeholders.

- Practical experience coordinating risk workshops and contributing to risk processes, with motivation to deepen analytical capability.

- Comfortable working in fast‑paced, high‑volume project settings with clear, structured communication skills.

Manager-level:
- Leads risk reviews and QRA/QSRA delivery, presenting confidently to senior stakeholders and operating autonomously across multiple projects.

- Sets and assures risk frameworks, governance processes and analytical standards across programmes or portfolios.

- Coaches and uplifts team capability while shaping portfolio‑level risk strategy and providing expert challenge.

We plan and orchestrate delivery for complex transport and energy programmes—bringing together first‑principles planning with 4D/5D digital delivery, data analytics and connected platforms. Our planners combine P6 mastery with digital twins, 4D simulation and linear planning to build credible sequences, stress‑test constraints, and generate data‑driven insights that accelerate decisions across portfolios.

We’re hiring industry specialists to push beyond “P6‑only” planning. You’ll leverage BIM‑integrated schedules, 4D visualisation, QSRA, and predictive forecasting to challenge and improve construction sequences from first principles—grounded in productivity rates, access regimes and logistics. You will set programme planning strategy, standards and digital ways of working across suppliers and contracts.

Planning & Scheduling (Core)

- Prepare baselines, change updates and time‑impact analyses aligned to NEC/FIDIC or client standards; maintain critical path and float integrity.

- Produce clear narratives, data‑rich look‑aheads and recovery options for leaders.

First‑Principles & Constructability (Manager emphasis)
- Build/challenge schedules from first principles using method statements, crew mixes and validated productivity rates (per shift, possession/outage).

- Stress‑test sequences against logistics, access/traffic management, outage regimes and vendor lead‑times; optimise through 4D simulation and linear planning where applicable.

- Influence construction strategy and commissioning logic with evidence‑based insight.

Integration with Cost, Risk & Change
- Align schedule with cost estimates, risk registers and procurement; maintain traceability to milestones, BoQs and control budgets.

- Support QSRA and time‑risk allowances; feed risk outcomes into re‑sequencing and recovery.

- Administer schedule change control; quantify delay/acceleration and support commercial teams.

Reporting, Governance & Stakeholders
- Provide dashboards, S‑curves and performance indices; communicate critical issues and recovery paths in plain, visual language.

- Facilitate collaborative planning with client, design, contractors and third parties.

- (Manager) Chair programme reviews and drive planning standards across suppliers.

Continuous Improvement & Standards
- Apply recognised schedule health checks (constraints, lags, open ends, negative float) and defensible assumptions.

- Capture lessons on productivity and access strategies; maintain standard libraries (norms, typical sequences).

- Contribute to planning methods, templates and training, including 4D/5D and data pipelines to dashboards.

Experience we are looking for:
Essential:
- Demonstrated industry planning/scheduling experience (preferably transport and/or energy).

- Strong Primavera P6 capability, building and maintaining schedules, progress updates and report development.

- Proven grasp of construction methods and productivity rates.

- Confident communicator and skilled at stakeholder management.

- Eager to deepen first‑principles and QSRA/4D skills.

Manager-level:
- Experience leading collaborative planning, challenging from first principles, triangulating durations with norms/crews and supporting QSRA/time‑impact.

- Owning programme planning strategy and standards, integrating schedule with cost/risk/procurement and setting digital planning ways of working.

- Leading and mentoring teams.

Set yourself apart with NEC/FIDIC familiarity, QSRA, TILOS/linear planning, Synchro/4D, Power BI analytics, multi‑country exposure.

Lead the future of planning—from 4D/5D and digital twins to portfolio analytics—while shaping Ireland’s energy transition and transport modernisation, with global learning and clear progression.

jobs.title: Global Network - Strategy - M&A and Private Equity Consulting – Senior Manager / Manager
jobs.description:
Join Accenture Strategy's Global Network - M&A and Private Equity Consulting team, a high-impact practice that helps leading Private Equity investors and corporate clients shape, evaluate, and execute complex transactions. As a Manager, you will operate at the intersection of strategy, execution, and value creation across the full deal lifecycle - from target screening and diligence to Day 1 readiness, integration, separation, and portfolio transformation.
You will lead complex M&A and PE engagements, own senior client relationships, and guide teams through high-velocity deal environments. This is an entrepreneurial, market-facing role for leaders who combine structured problem solving, commercial judgment, and hands-on delivery to help grow Accenture's M&A and Private Equity practice across geographies.

- Lead end-to-end execution and governance of complex M&A and PE engagements spanning pre-deal diligence, deal execution, Day 1 readiness, integration, separation, and value creation.
- Shape workplans, hypotheses, deliverables, and executive-ready recommendations for ambiguous transaction and transformation priorities.
- Drive senior client conversations, workshops, steering committee updates, and C-suite / Investment Committee-ready presentations.
- Manage engagement risks, timelines, quality, and team performance while balancing commercial outcomes with delivery excellence.
- Build trusted relationships with PE firms, corporate clients, account teams, industry / functional teams, and global M&A / PE leadership to originate and convert opportunities.
- Lead RFPs, proposals, client orals, account development, IP creation, and thought leadership to strengthen Accenture's market presence in M&A and Private Equity.
- Mentor consultants, build high-performing teams, and create an environment that promotes ownership, apprenticeship, and growth.

Functional M&A: Lead Commercial / Operational Due Diligence, Target Screening, synergy and value creation assessment, operating model design, and Functional Integration / Separation planning and execution across Finance, Supply Chain, Procurement, HR, Commercial, and Operating Model workstreams.

Tech / IT M&A: Lead Technology, Cybersecurity, and Platform Due Diligence, as well as IT Integration / Separation strategy and execution across applications, infrastructure, data, cybersecurity, cloud / ERP platforms, TSA planning, and technology operating model.

Must-Have
- 6+ years/10+ years of post-MBA experience in M&A consulting, strategy consulting, transaction advisory, Private Equity, or a comparable deal environment.
- Demonstrated leadership in either Functional M&A or Tech / IT M&A across diligence, integration, separation, or portfolio value creation.
- Proven experience managing senior client stakeholders, engagement teams, governance forums, and executive-level deliverables.
- Strong commercial acumen, structured problem-solving, deal judgment, and ability to translate complex analysis into board-level recommendations.
- Experience contributing to business development, proposals, client orals, account shaping, or pipeline conversion in an M&A / transaction advisory context.
- Deep industry knowledge in one or more priority sectors: CMT, Financial Services, Resources, Healthcare / Life Sciences, Consumer Goods & Services, or Retail.
- Ability to lead in fast-paced, ambiguous, deadline-driven deal environments while coaching consultants and managing quality.
- Experience in Day 1 readiness, IMO / SMO setup, TSA management, synergy tracking, and separation governance.
- Experience working across multi-geography, cross-functional teams and with global delivery / offshore networks.

Good to Have
- Experience in GCC strategy, setup, scaling, optimization, or transformation initiatives.
- Exposure to AI-led transformation, analytics, automation, or digital enablement in a deal, transaction, or portfolio value creation context.
- Portfolio value creation, synergy realization, EBITDA improvement, or ESG strategy experience in a PE-backed context.

- Project Workstream Execution: Collaborate with managers to define deliverables, lead workstreams, manage timelines, and ensure high-quality outputs

- Functional M&A: Must have hands-on experience in post-deal execution, including integration/separation of functions
- Engagement Support: Prepare client decks, support RFPs and thought capital development

Industry Focus (Preferred)

CMT, Financial Services, Resources, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Consumer Goods & Services, Retail

- Strong problem-solving and analytical capabilities with issue-based thinking
- Experience in direct client interactions, including presenting findings and driving stakeholder discussions.

- Business acumen and knowledge of M&A trends, investment models, and PE-backed transformation mandates

S&C GN - Tech Strategy & Transformation - Tech M&A - Senior Manager
jobs.description:
Senior Manager – Technology M&A Advisory

Join our team in Technology Strategy & Transformation for an exciting opportunity to help leading global organizations navigate the technology dimensions of mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, carve-outs, and joint ventures.

Practice: Technology Strategy & Transformation, Global Network | Area of Work: Technology M&A | Level: Senior Manager | Location: Bangalore/Gurgaon/Mumbai/Pune/Chennai/Hyderabad/Kolkata | Years of Experience: 12–18 years

Explore an Exciting Career at Accenture

Do you enjoy solving complex business and technology challenges? Are you passionate about helping clients create value through successful integrations and separations? Do you thrive in fast-paced transaction environments and enjoy partnering with C-suite executives to drive critical business outcomes?

Then this is the right place for you.

The Practice – A Brief Sketch

The Technology M&A team helps clients navigate the technology implications of mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, carve-outs, joint ventures, and business transformations. We work across the transaction lifecycle, with a strong focus on post-deal signing activities including sign-to-close planning, Day 1 readiness, integration planning, separation planning, TSA strategy and exit planning, and execution through Integration Management Offices (IMO) and Separation Management Offices (SMO).

Our professionals help clients identify and realize transaction value while managing technology risks, operational dependencies, and transformation opportunities. We work closely with executive leadership, business stakeholders, and technology teams to design and execute integration and separation strategies that enable successful transaction outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead large-scale Technology M&A programs across mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, carve-outs, and joint ventures.
• Serve as a trusted advisor to C-suite and senior technology executives on transaction-related technology decisions.
• Lead sign-to-close planning, Day 1 readiness, integration planning, separation planning, TSA strategy, and TSA exit execution.
• Oversee Integration Management Office (IMO) and Separation Management Office (SMO) governance, execution, and value realization activities.
• Define technology integration and separation strategies across applications, infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, data, ERP, and operating models.
• Drive synergy identification, value capture, risk mitigation, and transaction execution planning.
• Lead multi-disciplinary consulting teams and provide overall engagement leadership, quality assurance, and stakeholder management.
• Build executive-level business cases, steering committee materials, and transformation roadmaps.
• Support business development, proposal creation, thought leadership, and practice growth initiatives.
• Develop and mentor managers and consultants within the Technology M&A practice.

Bring Your Best Skills Forward

• Deep experience leading Technology M&A engagements including integrations, separations, carve-outs, Day 1 readiness, TSA management, and post-merger integration programs.
• Strong executive presence with the ability to influence senior business and technology stakeholders.
• Proven ability to manage large, complex, global programs with multiple workstreams and stakeholder groups.
• Strong commercial acumen and experience supporting sales, account growth, and client relationship development.
• Ability to translate transaction objectives into actionable technology strategies and execution plans.

Technology Domain Experience

Candidates should possess practical experience in at least one of the following technology domains and understand how these capabilities evolve during M&A transactions, integrations, and separations:

1. IT Infrastructure & Cloud
• Infrastructure integration and separation planning.
• Cloud migration and cloud operating model considerations.
• Data center, network, workplace, hosting, and end-user computing environments.
• Infrastructure TSA planning and exit execution.

2. ERP
• Experience with SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, or similar ERP platforms.
• ERP integration, harmonization, migration, or carve-out activities.
• Understanding of business process impacts, reporting, controls, and data migration considerations during transactions.

3. Enterprise Architecture & IT Operating Model Transformation
• Enterprise architecture assessments and target-state design.
• Application portfolio rationalization and technology roadmap development.
• IT operating model design and transformation.
• Technology governance, capability models, and organizational design considerations during integrations and separations.

Candidates should possess a strong understanding of how technology environments, operating models, applications, and infrastructure are impacted during mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and carve-outs. They should be comfortable advising clients on transaction implications, identifying risks and dependencies, and shaping integration and separation strategies across the deal lifecycle.

What’s in it for You?

• Opportunity to work on high-profile global M&A transactions and transformative business programs.
• Exposure to senior client executives and strategic decision-making processes.
• Collaboration with leading practitioners across Technology Strategy, M&A, Enterprise Architecture, Cloud, Cybersecurity, and Industry groups.
• Personalized training and development programs to strengthen transaction, consulting, and leadership capabilities.
• A diverse and inclusive culture focused on innovation, growth, and continuous learning.

About Accenture:
Accenture is a leading global professional services company, providing a broad range of services and solutions in strategy, consulting, digital, technology and operations. Combining unmatched experience and specialized skills across more than 40 industries and all business functions — underpinned by the world’s largest delivery network — Accenture works at the intersection of business and technology to help clients improve their performance and create sustainable value for their stakeholders. With 569,000 people serving clients in more than 120 countries, Accenture drives innovation to improve the way the world works and lives. Visit us at www.accenture.com

About Accenture Strategy & Consulting:
Accenture Strategy shapes our clients’ future, combining deep business insight with the understanding of how technology will impact industry and business models. Our focus on issues such as digital disruption, redefining competitiveness, operating and business models as well as the workforce of the future helps our clients find future value and growth in a digital world. Today, digital is changing the way organizations engage with their employees, business partners, customers and communities. This is our unique differentiator. To bring this global perspective to our clients, Accenture Strategy's services include those provided by our Capability Network – a distributed management consulting organization that provides management consulting and strategy expertise across the client lifecycle. Our Capability Network teams complement our in-country teams to deliver cutting-edge expertise and measurable value to clients all around the world. For more information visit https://www.accenture.com/us-en/Careers/capability-network

As a team:
The Health & Public Sector Industry and Enterprise team are working at the centre of high-profile transformations across the UK government and healthcare sectors. Within the practice, you will work on innovative projects with colleagues and clients to drive excellence from strategy through to implementation, making changes that directly impact citizens. You will be using the latest technologies and methodologies with clients to help them achieve tangible outcomes and accelerate value. Do you want to work in an environment that is cutting-edge, collaborative and challenging, doing work that really matters?
This is a specialist role within our Health practice, focused on healthcare transformation for clients including NHS organisations, integrated care systems, arm's length bodies, and private health providers. We are looking for people who combine strong consulting and advisory skills with a genuine understanding of healthcare from the inside — those who have worked in or alongside clinical settings and bring that perspective to bear on some of the most complex transformation challenges in the UK health system.
You'll learn, grow and advance in a collaborative culture that thrives on shared success, diverse ways of thinking and enables boundaryless opportunities that can drive your career in new and exciting ways. At Accenture, you can truly take control of your own career.
If you're looking for a challenging career working in a vibrant environment with access to training and a global network of experts, this could be the role for you.

In our team you will learn:
- How to develop and deliver solutions to real world problems, partnering with clients to achieve positive outcomes through collaboration

- How to maximise the use of data in everything you do, using this data to drive solutions and tell meaningful stories to our clients

- How to lead with user-centricity at the heart of our work

- To obsess about driving value for your clients

As a Health & Public Sector Consulting Manager, you will:
- Work on projects across a range of health and care clients, including NHS organisations, arm's length bodies, integrated care systems, private health clients, research and regulatory bodies

- Be the face of Accenture to the client in your engagements, working with senior stakeholders to advise, challenge and coach as needed

- Develop detailed understanding of your client's business and drive issue-based discussions grounded in a clear understanding of client challenges and barriers

- Cultivate trust-based client relationships

- Identify and address client business issues through root cause analysis and by applying pragmatic, results-driven problem-solving techniques and creative insights

- Use a human-centred approach to solve problems, frame opportunities, and achieve innovation through collaboration and co-creation

- Own streams of complex work that meets client expectations on delivering value-centric, data-driven outcomes

- Lead teams to deliver excellence to the client

- Be a people leader, creating an environment your people want to work in, and managing the day to day work of your team

We are looking for experience in the following skills:
The most important thing for us is that you display the right attitude. We would like you to actively contribute to our community and clients as a practitioner, think logically to tackle problems and engage others. We want you to be driven to develop yourself and others, an ability to see and articulate the bigger picture of how individual projects and deliverables create value for citizens and a passion for innovation and the latest technology trends. This role will require creative thinking, excellent client communication skills and the ability to identify new innovative ways to apply our skills and services to solve a wider set of client problems.
As well as the above, you should have experience/expertise in one or more of the following areas:
- Analytical problem-solving skills and continuous improvement techniques

- Strategic thinking skills and the ability to bring insight to complex problems

- Designing and/or implementing operating models

- Creating and/or managing complex business cases

- Working with data in the design or delivery of consulting services in the public sector

- Working with technology to design or deliver transformation of public services

- Strong interpersonal skills, with the capability to influence senior stakeholders

- Experience of working with public sector clients, either in government departments or health & care clients

- Experience driving new business in terms of strategy, relationships and identifying growth opportunities

- Experience in project & programme management methodologies and governance — including best practice industry techniques and frameworks (e.g. PRINCE2, MSP)

- Experience of delivering projects using Agile techniques and frameworks and the ability to lead Agile teams

- Ability to operate at all stages of a project/programme lifecycle, from proposal through to full programme delivery, and experience managing risks and working with senior client partners

- A background in clinical practice— this is a requirement for this role. We are looking for candidates who have direct experience of working in a clinical or healthcare delivery environment, whether through a current or previous professional registration, international clinical practice, or significant hands-on experience in a healthcare setting. You will bring an instinctive understanding of how health systems work, the pressures clinicians and operational teams face, and what good looks like from a patient and system perspective.

Set yourself apart:
This role is well suited to someone who has already made the transition from full-time clinical or NHS operational work into advisory, transformation, or strategy roles — and is now looking to bring that experience into a leading global consultancy. The ideal candidate will have spent a portion of their career outside of direct clinical delivery, developing the commercial, analytical, and client-facing skills that consulting demands, while retaining a genuine connection to and credibility within the healthcare world.
Backgrounds that tend to work well include:
- Experience in an NHS transformation, strategy, or improvement function (e.g. an ICS, NHS England, NHSE/I, or equivalent)

- Roles in a health arm's length body, regulator, or policy organisation (e.g. CQC, NICE, UKHSA, DHSC)

- Advisory or commercial roles within healthcare — such as health-focused management consulting, a health tech or medtech company, or a public health advisory organisation

- Academic or research roles with a strong applied or translational focus in health systems or health policy

You do not need to hold a current clinical registration to apply — we welcome candidates whose clinical experience was earlier in their career or gained in another country, provided you can demonstrate genuine clinical grounding and a strong track record in transformation, advisory, or change delivery since.
Additional differentiators we value:
- In-depth understanding of the specific healthcare or government landscapes you have worked in

jobs.description:
Accenture helps the world’s leading enterprises reinvent by building their digital core and unleashing the power of AI to create value at speed for organizations across industries. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI, and to be the most client-focused, AI-enabled, great place to work in the world. We bring together the talent of our approximately 799,000 people with proprietary assets and platforms, deep process and industry expertise, and leading ecosystem relationships to deliver end-to-end solutions and measurable outcomes at scale. We serve approximately 9,000 clients and generated approximately $70 billion in FY25 revenue. Visit us at accenture.com .

ABOUT THE PRACTICE
Higher education is in the middle of one of the most significant operational transformations it has seen in decades. Institutions are rethinking how they manage finance, HR, payroll, procurement, and research administration, moving away from legacy systems and fragmented processes toward integrated platforms that can support the pace and complexity of a modern university or college. All of this while the promise and reality of AI is changing the way we deliver and the opportunities for functional transformation inside and outside of the ERP.

The stakes are real. These are not back-office projects. They touch every faculty member, every department administrator, every researcher managing a grant, every employee waiting on a paycheck. Done well, they unlock institutional capacity that was previously buried in manual processes and disconnected systems. Done poorly, they create disruption that takes years to recover from.
Our Education practice is at the forefront in driving this reinvention -  working with universities, four-year colleges, and community colleges on the strategy, readiness, and implementations that matter most to them. If this market excites you and you have the experience to make a difference in it, we would like to meet you.

THE WORK

As a higher education transformation lead, you combine higher education functional expertise with the ability to lead complex, technology-enabled institutional transformation, from strategy and readiness through design, implementation, stabilization, and value realization. We are seeking individuals that have demonstrated this through overall program delivery or deep experience in specific functional domains such as Finance, HR, payroll, procurement, or research administration is where you built your career and where your credibility lives.

Higher education implementations fail for predictable reasons, and they are almost never about the technology. They fail because the complexity of decentralized operating models was underestimated. Because change management in a shared governance environment was treated as a communications exercise instead of a sustained engagement strategy. Because the research enterprise was bolted on late instead of designed for from the start. Because integration dependencies with student systems, advancement platforms, and research administration tools were discovered in testing instead of scoped in design. Because data migration, including payroll history, grant encumbrances, and position control records, was underplanned and politically underestimated.

The practitioners we are looking for understand all of this before the project kickoff. We are looking for:  Finance leaders who knows that a university close cycle feeds board materials and rating agency disclosures, and designs accordingly. HR leaders who have navigated shared governance and built adoption strategies that actually work with faculty and department administrators. Research Administration leaders who understand effort reporting, indirect cost recovery, and federal sponsor compliance as deeply as they understand the platform. Payroll or Procurement leaders who has designed for the real institutional environment, not the simplified version.

You will own senior client relationships in your domain, lead high-stakes engagements, work collaboratively across the teams and for our clients, help shape markets before the RFP is written, and raise the functional quality of everything the team delivers.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Lead Cloud ERP engagements – with a lens on business transformation - for college and university clients, either as an overall delivery lead or as the senior owner of the functional tower in your domain, with accountability for quality, client relationships, and outcomes.

- Own senior client relationships in your functional area, including the VP of Finance, CFO, CHRO, VP of Research, Sponsored Programs Director, Payroll Director, and Chief Procurement Officer, engaging as a peer who understands what they are managing, not just what they have asked for.

- Drive functional design decisions that account for the full complexity of how higher education institutions actually operate: decentralized finance and HR structures, shared governance dynamics, research enterprise requirements, cross-functional integration dependencies, and board reporting obligations.

- Lead change management strategy within your domain, building adoption approaches that work in a shared governance culture, engage department-level administrators and faculty stakeholders, and account for the political realities of institutional transformation.

- Own integration strategy within your tower, understanding how your functional domain connects to student systems, research platforms, advancement systems, state reporting environments, and other enterprise tools, and ensuring those dependencies are designed for, not discovered late.
- Bring AI-assisted delivery, platform-native AI capabilities and responsible workflow automation into engagements as standard practice, and help clients think through what governed AI adoption looks like in their institutional context. Outside of ERP toolsets, bring modernization and functional opportunities for AI-process redesign and automation.

- Contribute to must-win pursuits and proposals, bringing the kind of domain credibility that changes what a higher education evaluator thinks of us in the room because they can tell within the first ten minutes whether someone understands their institution or is pitching a generic playbook.

- Help shape the market 24 to 36 months before an RFP: build relationships with university functional leaders, engage with platform account teams on joint pipeline, and represent the practice at NACUBO, EDUCAUSE, CUPA-HR and related forums.

- Contribute to practice development including solutions, services, and client outcomes for use on future engagements.

- Develop junior and mid-level practitioners in your functional area, helping them build the domain depth, change management instincts, and platform fluency that make the whole team more credible.

Travel: Ability to travel 50%+

WHAT YOU NEED
Required:
- Minimum 8 years of consulting or functional experience in higher education or community college environments with Senior-level functional expertise in at least one domain: institutional finance and budget operations, HR and academic workforce management, payroll administration, procurement and purchasing compliance, or research administration and sponsored programs.

- Minimum 7 years of hands-on delivery experience with Cloud ERP in a functional capacity with demonstrated experience as a delivery lead or senior functional tower owner on large, complex ERP engagements or similar institution-wide transformations and implementations in higher education, with accountability for design quality, senior relationships, and outcomes in your domain.

Preferred:
- Demonstrated experience engaging directly with senior functional executives in higher education organizations.
- Prior experience in a senior functional operating role within a college, university, or community college, such as VP of Finance, CFO, CHRO, VP of Research, Sponsored Programs Director, Payroll Director, or Chief Procurement Officer. People who have sat in the chair.

- Finance: Cloud ERP Financials delivery experience in a higher education context. Deep familiarity with enrollment-driven budgeting, all funds budgeting, GASB fund accounting, endowment management, and the board and audit committee reporting cycles that govern institutional finance. Experience designing for decentralized college and departmental finance structures.

- HR: Cloud ERP HCM delivery experience with depth in academic workforce structures, faculty appointment management, or large-scale HR transformation in higher education. Experience developing adoption strategies that work in a shared governance environment, engaging faculty governance bodies, department chairs, and distributed HR functions.

- Payroll: Cloud ERP Payroll delivery experience with multi-bargaining-unit complexity, faculty and staff pay structures, or college and university payroll compliance at scale.

- Procurement: Cloud ERP Procurement delivery experience with familiarity with higher education purchasing compliance, decentralized requisition-to-pay environments, and the intersection of procurement and sponsored programs, including grant-funded purchasing compliance under federal regulations.

- Research Administration: deep familiarity with sponsored programs finance and operations in a higher education context, including effort reporting, indirect cost recovery (F&A rates), sub-award management, cost transfer processes, grant lifecycle management, and federal sponsor compliance (NIH, NSF, DoD, 2 CFR 200). Experience designing ERP or research administration systems to support the full sponsored research lifecycle, and working across the sponsored programs office, finance, and faculty principal investigators.

- Experience managing data migration complexity in higher education, including payroll history, grant encumbrances, position control records, and other sensitive institutional data that requires both technical rigor and careful stakeholder management.

- Experience with integration design in complex higher education environments, connecting ERP platforms to student systems, advancement platforms, research administration tools, state reporting systems, or other enterprise applications.

- Experience contributing to competitive higher education pursuits, including pre-RFP positioning, institutional advisory relationships, and engagement with platform account teams. Familiarity with the higher education procurement and RFP process from the client side is a significant differentiator.

- Bachelor's degree preferred. Equivalent experience considered.

jobs.title: CG&S Growth Strategy and Enterprise Reinvention - Strategy Principal Director
jobs.description:
We Are
Accenture's Consumer Goods & Services practice helps the world's leading brands reinvent how they grow, compete, and operate. We work with food and beverage, beauty and personal care, household products, consumer health, pet care, and agribusiness clients at the intersection of enterprise strategy, commercial growth, operating model reinvention, M&A and integration, and AI-enabled decision making. We combine industry depth with strategy, technology, operations, data, and talent capabilities to turn CEO-level priorities into measurable revenue, margin, and enterprise-value outcomes.

You Are
A senior strategy leader who combines top-tier consulting experience with senior operating experience building and scaling growth engines. You have led enterprise growth strategy, portfolio and business model decisions, commercial and operating model transformations, and M&A or integration agendas. You understand consumer brands, product and innovation economics, customer and consumer needs, and how growth choices translate into execution across marketing, sales, operations, technology, and talent. You are comfortable advising CEOs and executive teams, shaping an ambiguous question into a fact-based value case and actionable roadmap, and staying accountable through execution. You can originate work, mobilize cross-functional teams, and develop leaders while maintaining high standards for quality and commercial outcomes.

The Work
As an Associate Director, you will lead CEO- and C-suite-level strategy and reinvention engagements for Consumer Goods clients. You will shape and sell work, lead multi-workstream delivery, and help clients convert growth, portfolio, integration, and operating-model priorities into measurable results.

Executive and Engagement Leadership
- Lead large, complex strategy and enterprise-reinvention programs with multiple concurrent workstreams and senior stakeholder groups.
- Own relationships with client CEOs, business-unit presidents, CFOs, CMOs, Chief Sales Officers, COOs, CSCOs, and strategy or corporate-development leaders.
- Translate ambiguous executive questions into testable hypotheses, focused workplans, executive decisions, and sequenced transformation roadmaps.
- Orchestrate cross-functional teams spanning strategy, finance and value, commercial, operations, data and AI, technology, talent, and change management.
- Ensure engagement quality, timeliness, financial performance, and risk management; resolve escalations and maintain alignment across differing stakeholder perspectives.

Growth Strategy and Enterprise Reinvention
- Define enterprise and business-unit growth strategies, market and category choices, portfolio priorities, and business-model options.
- Build growth engines spanning consumer and customer strategy, brand and innovation, commercial excellence, pricing and revenue growth management, route-to-market, partnerships, and new ventures.
- Design operating models, decision rights, governance, organization structures, capabilities, and performance-management systems required to execute the strategy.
- Develop fact-based value cases, scenario models, revenue and margin bridges, investment priorities, and benefit-realization plans.
- Shape reinvention programs around Accenture's Consumer Goods priorities, including the Enterprise Performance Engine, Connected Sales Reinvention, and Insight-to-Launch.
- Apply sub-industry nuance across food and beverage, beauty and personal care, household products, consumer health, pet care, and agribusiness to tailor recommendations to client-specific economics and routes to market.

M&A, Integration, and Portfolio Transformation
- Advise clients on strategic alternatives, portfolio reshaping, partnerships, acquisitions, divestitures, and inorganic-growth priorities.
- Lead integration strategy, growth-synergy identification, Day 1 and Day 2 operating-model design, and value-capture planning.
- Protect brand, customer, and talent momentum while integrating commercial, operational, technology, and corporate capabilities.
- Establish integration governance, decision forums, metrics, and value-tracking mechanisms that connect transaction logic to realized outcomes.

AI, Data, and Digital Growth Enablement
- Identify where AI, analytics, and data can unlock growth, improve decision quality, accelerate innovation, and increase enterprise productivity.
- Translate priority use cases into the process, operating-model, data, technology, governance, and workforce changes required for enterprise adoption.
- Use GenAI and agentic tools to accelerate research, consumer and customer insight, strategy development, scenario planning, and executive decision support.
- Partner with AI, data, technology, and ecosystem teams to move solutions from proof of concept to scaled business impact with responsible-AI controls.

Business Development and Practice Growth
- Originate and shape Consumer Goods strategy and reinvention opportunities, including C-suite sessions, proposals, solution architectures, value cases, and commercial models.
- Lead pursuit teams, coordinate account and offering stakeholders, and maintain momentum from initial executive dialogue through a funded mandate.
- Build reusable assets, case studies, thought leadership, and market points of view that strengthen the Consumer Goods growth-strategy proposition.
- Coach, mentor, and develop managers and consultants; contribute to recruiting, staffing, performance management, and succession planning.
- Support account planning and pipeline development across priority North American Consumer Goods clients.

Principal Directors have:
- Executive presence and the ability to lead fact-based, decision-oriented discussions with C-suite and Board-level stakeholders.
- Deep capability in enterprise and growth strategy, commercial strategy, operating-model design, portfolio choices, and value creation.
- Ability to lead large, multi-workstream programs and mobilize cross-functional teams across strategy, technology, operations, and talent.
- Strong client relationship management, business development, negotiation, and stakeholder-alignment skills.
- Advanced problem-solving, financial and strategic analysis, synthesis, and business judgment.
- Ability to convert complex analysis into clear executive narratives, choices, and actionable roadmaps.
- Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-moving situations and resolving issues and risks proactively.
- Ability to coach senior team members, build high-performing teams, and create an inclusive, accountable working environment.
- Willingness to travel up to 50%, based on client and project needs.

Basic Qualifications:
- Minimum of 12 years of relevant professional experience.
- Bachelor's degree or a minimum of 12 years of equivalent professional experience.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in strategy consulting, professional services, or an equivalent internal corporate-strategy role.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in one or more of the following: enterprise or growth strategy, corporate development, commercial strategy, business-model design, M&A and integration, or operating-model transformation.
- Minimum of 3 years of experience leading complex, multi-workstream strategy or transformation programs and managing teams.
- Minimum of 3 years of experience working directly with C-suite or senior executive stakeholders.
- Minimum of 2 years of experience shaping consulting engagements, proposals, or executive-sponsored business cases.

Preferred:
- MBA or equivalent advanced degree.
- Demonstrated Consumer Goods or consumer-facing industry experience in one or more of the following: brand or product strategy, innovation, marketing, sales, commercial growth, portfolio strategy, or business-unit leadership.
- Experience developing financial and strategic value cases and linking recommendations to implementation and benefit realization.
- Working knowledge of current AI, data, digital-commerce, and technology trends and how they apply to Consumer Goods growth and operating-model challenges.
- Prior senior operating role in strategy, growth, integration, corporate development, marketing, business development, or commercial leadership.
- Prior Accenture experience or experience at a leading strategy or management consulting firm.
- Experience across one or more Consumer Goods sub-industries, including food and beverage, beauty and personal care, household products, consumer health, pet care, or agribusiness.
- Experience leading post-merger integration, growth-synergy capture, portfolio transformation, or strategic-partnership programs.
- Experience with revenue growth management, customer strategy, route-to-market, new ventures, or ecosystem-enabled growth.
- Hands-on experience leveraging AI tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, or Gemini in a professional environment.
- Experience leading enterprise initiatives across multiple business units, geographies, or functional organizations.

- Build and maintain strong working relationships with client functional leaders in your domain, such as VPs of Finance, Controllers, HR Directors, Payroll Directors, Chief Procurement Officers, Sponsored Programs Directors, or Grants Managers, and engage with them as a peer who understands their world.

- Lead stakeholder engagement and change management within your tower, recognizing that adoption in higher education requires navigating shared governance, decentralized departmental cultures, and stakeholders who will scrutinize every design decision.

- Navigate integration complexity by understanding how your tower connects to other enterprise systems, student platforms, research administration systems, and state or federal reporting environments, and by designing with those dependencies in mind.

- Apply AI-assisted analysis, workflow design, and delivery acceleration as part of how you work day to day, not as an add-on but as a standard method that improves quality and speed.

- Communicate clearly on status, risk, and decisions to senior stakeholders, including awareness of how implementation milestones interact with board reporting cycles and audit timelines.

- Contribute to proposals and pursuits by bringing domain credibility that resonates with higher education evaluators who are looking for practitioners that understand their institution, not just their software.

Travel: Ability to travel 50%+.

WHAT YOU NEED
Required:

- Minimum 5 years of consulting or functional experience in higher education or community college environments with deep functional expertise in at least one domain: institutional finance and budget operations, HR and academic workforce management, payroll administration, procurement and purchasing compliance, or research administration and sponsored programs.

- Minimum 5 years of hands-on delivery experience with a Cloud ERP platform in a functional or technical capacity with experience leading a functional tower or workstream on a large-scale ERP engagement, with responsibility for design, delivery, and client engagement within your domain.

Preferred:
- Bachelor's degree
- Finance: experience with enrollment-driven budget modeling, GASB fund accounting, endowment accounting, or board and audit committee reporting in a Cloud ERP Financials context. Familiarity with how decentralized college and departmental finance structures affect system design.

- HR: experience with faculty appointment structures, academic workforce planning, classification and compensation, or HR transformation in a Cloud ERP HCM context. Experience navigating shared governance environments and designing for both centralized HR and distributed departmental HR functions.

- Payroll: experience with multi-bargaining-unit payroll configuration, faculty and staff pay structures, or complex leave and benefit plans in a Cloud ERP Payroll context.

- Procurement: experience with higher education purchasing compliance, requisition-to-pay processes, grant-funded procurement, or the intersection of procurement and sponsored programs in a Cloud ERP Procurement context.

- Research Administration: experience with sponsored programs finance, effort reporting, indirect cost recovery, sub-award management, cost transfer processes, or grant lifecycle management in a higher education ERP or research administration system context. Familiarity with federal sponsor requirements (NIH, NSF, DoD) and 2 CFR 200 compliance as they apply to system design.

- Prior experience working within a college, university, or community college in a finance, HR, payroll, procurement, or sponsored programs function, with an understanding of the institution from the inside.

- Experience with data migration complexity in higher education, including payroll history, position control records, grant encumbrances, or other sensitive historical data that requires careful conversion strategy.

- Familiarity with AI-assisted delivery methods or platform-native AI capabilities in Cloud ERP platforms.

jobs.title: Strategy Consultant - Commodity Markets
jobs.description:
Role: Strategy Consultant, Commodity Markets
Level: Consultant
Location: Bangkok, Thailand
Practice: Accenture Commodity Markets, CEO Advisory
About Accenture
Accenture helps the world's leading organisations reinvent themselves, building their digital core and putting AI to work to create value at speed. We bring together approximately 799,000 people with proprietary assets and platforms, deep industry and process expertise, and leading ecosystem relationships. Our Reinvention Services span Cybersecurity, Digital Core, Finance, Industry and Enterprise, Song, Supply Chain and Engineering, and Talent, with advanced capability in AI and Data, Industry and Process, and Technology. We serve approximately 9,000 clients in more than 120 countries, with offices and operations in 52 countries and more than 200 cities, and reported revenues of approximately US$70 billion in fiscal 2025. Visit us at www.accenture.com.
About Accenture CEO Advisory
Accenture CEO Advisory works with chief executives, boards and their leadership teams on the decisions that set enterprise direction: where to compete, what to own, how to fund a shift in the portfolio, and what the operating model has to become to support it. The work sits upstream of execution but is judged on whether it survives contact with it, so we pair industry depth with the quantitative, technology and delivery capability to pressure-test an answer before a client commits capital behind it.
About Accenture Commodity Markets
Accenture Commodity Markets (ACM), part of Accenture CEO Advisory, is a global practice operating across multiple industries. It is one of the few global strategy practices offering a steep cross-industry learning curve alongside genuinely global project experience, working with organisations focused on commodity production, trading, logistics and marketing.
We combine industry knowledge across energy, chemicals, soft commodities, agriculture, metals, mining, utilities, transportation and consumer goods with analytics-led core strategy consulting, digital and AI capability.
Within Accenture we are known for the variety and complexity of the problems we take on, a close-knit global team, early responsibility for our people, rapid career progression and international exposure, having delivered projects in over 25 countries.
Our solution areas are:
Investment and Asset Portfolio Optimisation: portfolio strategy, capital allocation, long-term market modelling, M&A support, and integrated optimisation across physical and financial positions. Trading and Market Optimisation: trading strategy, positioning and risk management through advanced analytics, real-time insight, hedging, algorithmic trading and P&L attribution. Commodity Markets Decision Platforms, Ecosystem and Execution: AI-enabled decision platforms, CTRM and ETRM selection, ecosystem partners (Salesforce, Palantir and others), data architecture, AI model development and automation. Enterprise Activation and Operational Readiness: making sure organisations are ready to operate, trade and optimise from day one, covering operating model design, go-live strategy and capability build-out. Commodity Sourcing and Exposure Management: sourcing, hedging and supplier strategy for commodity-exposed industries, optimising cost, risk and resilience under market volatility.
About the Role in Thailand
ACM in Thailand advises state enterprises, listed energy groups and large industrial corporates on decisions that set their direction for the next decade: how to position a portfolio through the energy transition, what gas and power market liberalisation does to a commercial model, whether an asset or an acquisition earns its cost of capital, and how to stand up the trading and commercial capability a deregulated market demands.
Regulatory and transition depth in the Thai and wider ASEAN energy system runs through most of that work. Third-party access regimes, tariff structures, PPA economics and market design are commercial questions for our clients, and we are expected to hold a defensible view on them.
We also build with AI as a matter of course. Market and competitor scans, document-heavy regulatory review and first-cut modelling run with GenAI in the workflow. That changes how much ground a small team can cover, and it raises the bar on what counts as analysis rather than description.
The Thailand team is small and growing. You will own a workstream and its client relationships early, and you will present your own work to client leadership.
Key Responsibilities
Client Delivery and Development
- Lead project workstreams to closure with limited supervision, from framing the question through to the recommendation you defend in front of the client.
- Work on engagements in Thailand and across Southeast Asia, with access to the ACM global staffing pool for projects further afield.
- Work in cross-office teams spanning ACM Thailand and global ACM, bringing structure and quantitative and qualitative rigour to problems across our solution areas.
- Build and own the analysis behind the answer: financial and operational models, market and asset economics, and the numerical modelling of energy and commodity markets.
- Run client interviews and workshops, build the materials, and hold your own in the conversation about approach and recommendation.
- Work across corporate and portfolio strategy, energy transition positioning, market liberalisation and regulatory response, trading and risk capability set-up, operating model design, commercial optimisation, investment valuation and financial structuring, and balance sheet analysis.
- Use GenAI tooling as a default part of how you work, and take responsibility for the quality of what comes out of it.
- Develop client relationships by staying close to how each client actually decides, and stay market relevant through thought leadership and taking fresh ideas to them unprompted.

Practice Building
- Contribute to ACM Thailand, global ACM and the wider Accenture CEO Advisory community, and to building ACM offerings, assets and thought leadership.
- Support business development by running industry and company research (competitor and market scanning, market fundamentals, financials, customers) and by building proposal materials.
- Coach analysts on your workstream, on both the analysis and how it is communicated.

Required Experience
- An undergraduate and master's degree from a leading academic institution.
- 3-6 years of professional experience in strategy consulting, or in a relevant commercial, strategy or corporate development role in industry.
- Strong quantitative skills and comfort owning a financial or operational model end to end, including the assumptions and their defensibility.
- Business case development and financial analysis, with fluency reading and interrogating financial statements.
- Structured, hypothesis-led problem solving, and the ability to take a position where the evidence is incomplete and say what would change it.
- Working proficiency with GenAI tools in analytical work, and the judgement to know where their output cannot be trusted.
- Professional fluency in Thai and English, written and spoken.
- Demonstrated ability to deliver high-quality output with multicultural teams under short timeframes.

Desirable
- AI capability that goes beyond tool use, combined with quantitative modelling and commodity market knowledge.
- Sector exposure in energy, utilities, chemicals, agriculture, or metals and mining.
- Understanding of the Thai and ASEAN energy sector and its regulatory institutions.
- Exposure to commodity trading, risk management, or investment and asset valuation.
- International study or work experience.

Location and Working Arrangements
- Based in Bangkok, Thailand.
- Travel across Southeast Asia and, for global staffing, further afield.
- Flexible working arrangements, with the expectation of client site presence where the engagement requires it.

Why Join Us
- The Thailand practice is small and in build phase, so you carry real scope from the first engagement and you are visible to practice leadership from the start.
- Direct exposure to C-suite and board-level decisions at some of Thailand's largest energy and industrial groups, on questions where the answer is genuinely open.
- Access to the ACM global staffing pool, so cross-border and cross-industry project experience does not require leaving the practice.
- Continuous coaching from senior colleagues in ACM Thailand and global ACM, with a specialisation path set out deliberately rather than left to whatever staffing throws up.
- Flexible work arrangements and a competitive rewards package.

Next Steps
If this sounds like the right role, career and company for you, click below to apply.

jobs.title: GBS RTR Operating Model (Consultant)
jobs.description:
About Finance Reinvention Partner

Accenture’s Finance Reinvention Partner helps CFOs and finance leaders reinvent how finance creates and protects enterprise value—bringing together strategy, operating model, data, AI and technology to improve performance, insight, control and execution. In the UK and Ireland, the practice combines finance strategy and transformation capabilities with the enterprise platforms that enable them, including SAP, Oracle, Workday and enterprise performance management solutions.
Our GBS and Operating Model team helps clients design and implement how finance and other enterprise services should be organised and delivered across retained functions, Global Business Services, Global Capability Centres, Centres of Excellence and external service providers. We support the full transformation journey—from strategy, value case and target operating model through detailed design, mobilisation, implementation, service management and continuous improvement—embedding data, automation and AI to create scalable, resilient and value-led operations.

Why this role

This role supports the redesign of how Record-to-Report (R2R) and controllership services are organised and governed across group and local finance, GBS/GCC, Centres of Excellence, outsourcing partners and technology. You will help clients improve close performance, accounting quality, controls and service delivery while preserving clear statutory and fiduciary accountability.
At its core, this is an operating-model and process-transformation role. The Consultant brings sufficient R2R depth to analyse current-state issues, develop credible design options and translate approved decisions into detailed process, control, service and technology requirements.

The expertise you'll bring

Relevant R2R and operating-model transformation experience. 4+ years in R2R, controllership, finance transformation, GBS/GCC, ERP-enabled change or consulting, with hands-on ownership of defined analysis or design deliverables and exposure to at least one R2R improvement or transformation through design and into implementation, readiness or service transition.
R2R and controllership depth. Practical knowledge of period-end close, journals, reconciliations, intercompany, fixed assets, consolidation and group reporting, statutory reporting, accounting policy, master data, internal controls and audit requirements, with the ability to connect process issues to operating-model choices.
GBS and service-delivery exposure. Experience supporting decisions on retained and local-finance versus GBS scope, Global Process Owner and Centre of Excellence roles, organisation, governance, service levels, interfaces, transition and continuous-improvement requirements, including BPO or managed services where relevant.
Technology and data fluency. Ability to understand how enterprise platforms, data and digital capabilities shape a GBS operating model—not just how individual systems work. Connect working knowledge of ERP-enabled R2R transformation and close, reconciliation, consolidation, workflow, process-mining and analytics capabilities.
Automation, AI and auditability. A working understanding of how automation and AI can reshape R2R activities, including journal preparation, reconciliation matching, exception detection, close orchestration and narrative reporting. You can help assess which activities are suitable for automation or AI enablement, where finance judgement and accountability must remain with people, and how roles, decision rights, hand-offs and exception management should change.
Client, team and sector capability. Strong facilitation and presentation skills, analysis, process-mapping, documentation and stakeholder management; confidence in contributing in client workshops and owning defined deliverables; and experience in Consumer Goods & Services, Utilities and/or Energy.

What you'll be accountable for

- Assess the current R2R operating model by analysing service scope, activity location, organisation and capacity, close performance, process variation, policies, controls, data, enabling systems, service measures and the root causes of operational pain.
- Support the development of the target R2R service model and activity-placement options across group or corporate controllership, local and statutory finance, GBS/GCC, Global Process Owners, Centres of Excellence and external service providers. Use evidence to assess value, feasibility, risk and implementation dependencies.
- Develop detailed operating-model and service-design deliverables for assigned R2R areas, covering activity scope, roles, decision rights, capacity, governance, controls, hand-offs and service interfaces. This may include areas such as general ledger and close, journals, reconciliations, intercompany, fixed assets, consolidation, group and statutory reporting, and master data, together with interfaces to P2P, O2C, Tax, Treasury and FP&A.
- Assess the implications of standardisation, automation and AI for the future operating model, including which activities can be automated or technology-enabled, where finance judgement and accountability must remain with people, and how roles, approvals, exception handling, controls and audit evidence should change.
- Translate operating-model decisions into clear business, data and control requirements for ERP, close and reconciliation tools, workflow, analytics, automation and AI. Work with technology, data, controls and architecture specialists to clarify requirements and support their traceability through solution design, testing and implementation.
- Contribute to R2R governance and service-management design, including process ownership, RACIs, SLAs and OLAs, performance and control measures, escalation routes, service-review forums and continuous-improvement routines.
- Build supporting analysis for the case for change, benefits and implementation roadmap, and contribute to transition planning, knowledge transfer, business readiness, control changes, training, testing, cutover and early-life stabilisation.
- Produce clear, client-ready deliverables and support focused workshops with finance, controllership, GBS and technology stakeholders. Manage your assigned outputs, risks and dependencies, collaborate across multidisciplinary teams, and contribute to proposals and reusable R2R assets.

jobs.title: AI SDLC Transformation Manager
jobs.description:
We Are:

Strategic Technology Effectiveness, part of Accenture's Technology Strategy & Transformation Organization. We rebuild how large enterprises define, design and govern software, and we design and implement the agentic software and processes that run it. That work changes the operating model an engineering organization runs on, the ways of working underneath it, and the tooling that makes both of those real.

We start with evidence. Cycle time, flow efficiency, WIP and throughput show where delivery stalls, and that diagnosis sets the target. What we design from it is AI-native by construction. We redesign intake and prioritization, so demand meets real capacity, and rebuild the path from request to release so planning, build, review, testing and deployment connect to each other instead of handing off through spreadsheets and status meetings.

Most of our build work sits upstream, where the cost of rework gets set: requirements generation, user story synthesis, design review, architecture validation. That means creator and reviewer agent patterns, tool-use orchestration, and multi-agent workflows on enterprise frameworks, with a working understanding of what each pattern costs in tokens and where it breaks. We treat the lifecycle as a system and a product itself - built to operate at a speed required for the AI era.

Then we make it stick . Engineering teams move to AI-augmented work and stay there, which is what separates a delivery organization where AI is how software gets made from the working pilot.  Practitioner depth in delivery operating models and AI, paired with Accenture's global platform and technology expertise , puts us in front of delivery organizations at a scale few firms reach.

You Are
The AI SDLC Transformation Manager guides enterprise clients on redesigning software delivery to be AI-native.  You've spent real time in software delivery , not just studying it. You know what broken looks like at the process level, and you know what good looks like when AI is woven in deliberately rather than bolted on.

The Work
This role applies flow metric analysis to surface waste in existing processes, designs future-state AI-native workflows, and builds agentic systems for upstream SDLC phases (define, design, requirements). The Advisor brings deep fluency in the evolving AI tooling landscape and translates what digitally native engineering organizations are doing into actionable roadmaps for enterprise clients.

Role-Specific Responsibilities:

- Value stream mapping and flow metric analysis (cycle time, flow efficiency, WIP, throughput) to identify waste in existing SDLC practices

- Design of AI-native to-be processes that restructure and accelerate how software is defined, designed, and governed

- Change management for engineering teams transitioning to AI-augmented workflows

- Strategy and d esign of agentic systems targeting upstream SDLC phases: requirements generation, user story synthesis, design review, and architecture validation

- Know how and where to use creator and reviewer agent patterns an d  the token impact of doing so.

- Model SDLC as a system, identifying feedback loops, bottlenecks, and second-order effects of process changes

- Cross-functional perspective spanning product, engineering, QA, security, and platform

- Ability to maintain fluency in the rapidly evolving AI tooling ecosystem (coding assistants, agentic platforms, evaluation frameworks, MCP/tool orchestration)

- Ongoing research practice tracking capability shifts, new model releases, and emerging practitioner patterns

- Expertise in what digitally native organizations are doing today and ability to translate those benchmarks into actionable roadmaps for enterprise clients

- Ability to influence clients to change and modernize processes that limit the positive impact of agentic ways of working and overall SDLC

Travel may be required for this role.  The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Here’s What You Need:

- Minimum of 5 years working across the full SDLC , requirements through release , with demonstrated ability to map, measure, and redesign delivery processes

- Minimum of 3 years of hands-on experience designing or building multi-agent or LLM-integrated systems, including prompt engineering, tool-use orchestration, or agentic application development

- Minimum of 3 years in a consulting or advisory capacity working with engineering organizations, ideally at enterprise scale (5,000+ employees or $1B+ revenue)

- Minimum of 3 years applying flow metrics (cycle time, WIP, throughput, flow efficiency) or value stream mapping as active diagnostic tools, not just frameworks you've presented on

- Minimum of 2 years working directly with AI/ML systems, LLMs, or agentic architectures in a professional, not just experimental , context

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience)

Bonus points if you have

- Hands-on experience with 2+ leading AI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Amazon Q Developer, Cody) in enterprise environments

- Experience designing lightweight LLM evals for AI-generated SDLC artifacts ( requirements docs, user stories, design reviews )

- Working knowledge of Model Context Protocol (MCP) and emerging tool orchestration standards

- Fluency in at least one major delivery methodology (Agile, SAFe , continuous delivery) with a clear point of view on where AI creates the most leverage

- Track record of presenting AI transformation strategies to VP- or C-level stakeholders and getting buy-in
